body:
multisession-tabs: the product's sharpest UX edge is that a NEW session starts signed out.

It must — an empty session strips the browser's cookies, otherwise the tab inherits whoever you already were and nothing is isolated. But a user who creates 'admin' and clicks 'use here' sees a login page and concludes the button is broken. Aman hit exactly this and asked 'is use here a different feature or what'.

The behaviour is correct and is pinned by spike/run-firstlogin.mjs (plain tab -> use here on an empty session -> sign in -> close -> reopen already signed in, 4/4 on the real app). What was missing was saying so, in all three places the user looks: an 'empty' chip on the session row, an explanation banner when acting on one, and an in-page badge reading '<name> · sign in to save'.

General lesson: when a correct behaviour looks like a failure, the fix is never only in the code — every surface that shows the thing has to narrate it.
